WP1 · Work package

Policy DSL / IR / signed bundle

A fixed way to write flight rules in a YAML or JSON file (Policy DSL), and the parsed in-memory form that other parts read (IR). The rules are packed into a signed bundle with a hash, so a flight can later be checked against the exact rules it used.

What the grant asks for

“a single, version-controlled, validatable representation that the Prefix Compiler and Safety Shield share”Grant, Policy DSL page

Main files: guardrail/models.py guardrail/bundle.py policies/ tools/wp1_roundtrip_kpi.py

Built

  • Rule types, with time windows

    Flight rules are written in YAML. The rule types include polygon no-fly zones, an altitude band, speed and climb limits, obstacle clearance, a stand-off from the followed subject, and 3D corridors, and any rule can carry a time window.

    guardrail/models.py policies/

  • A fingerprint for every policy

    Each policy has a full SHA-256 hash over its canonical JSON. Flight logs and KPI numbers carry it, so a result can be traced to the exact rules it was produced under.

    guardrail/models.py

  • Signed policy bundles

    A policy and its manifest are packed into a bundle signed with Ed25519. The loader refuses an unsigned, edited or forged bundle. Where the cryptography library is not installed, a pure-Python verifier checks the signature instead.

    guardrail/bundle.py policies/keys/trusted_signers.json

  • Pinned versions

    A lock file pins one hash per policy version. The Shield node, the SITL demo and the city demo can load a signed bundle instead of the YAML file.

    policies/policy.lock.json sitl/ros2_shield_node.py demo/follow_vlm.py

  • A schema and replay bundles

    A JSON Schema describes the Policy DSL, and a flight can be packed into a replay bundle that re-derives its own KPIs.

    policies/policy_dsl.schema.json guardrail/replay.py

Shown

  • Round trip and tamper refusal

    29 of 29 project policies load back from a signed bundle with the same hash, the same rules and a verified signature, and 29 of 29 tampered copies are refused. A loader that checked nothing would refuse 0 of 29.

    Reproduce: python tools/wp1_roundtrip_kpi.py

  • Every stored flight traceable

    When the full-length policy hash was introduced, all 76 stored flight manifests could be traced to the policy they flew with (76/76); with the hash as computed before, 34/76 could.

Next for this work package

  • Next October 2026 Policy layers (regulation, site, mission) and circle fences.
  • Next October – November 2026 Mid-flight policy updates (a moving no-fly zone, a time-window switch, a corridor swap) through a REST endpoint.
